prompt: Implement peakIndices to return the indices of all peaks: elements strictly greater than BOTH neighbors. The first and last elements are never peaks.
explanation: Looping i from 1 to a.length - 2 guarantees a[i - 1] and a[i + 1] both exist, which handles the ends-are-never-peaks rule and empty or tiny arrays for free. The peak test needs strict > on both sides so plateaus like {3, 3} never qualify. Since the peak count is unknown up front, indices are gathered into a worst-case-sized array and trimmed with Arrays.copyOf.
hints: Only indexes 1 through a.length - 2 can be peaks; a loop over that range never goes out of bounds.
The condition is a[i] > a[i - 1] && a[i] > a[i + 1] -- strictly greater on BOTH sides.
Collect matches into a temp array with a count, then trim with java.util.Arrays.copyOf(found, count).
